probe.reading: The two cells are one run until the stage first decides (the reset after Improvement Boost, 90,327.85); they part at that reset (the 4th of the probe's list: ×3.5 at 90,357.75, ×4 at 90,368.7). More Layers costs a FIXED 1e175 quirk energy, and every quirk reset zeroes the energy. ×4 made three resets between Improvement Boost and More Layers, the last at 93,082.6 holding 2.1e171 energy; its next was not due before that run crossed the price at 97,719.45 (a 4,637-s run). ×3.5 made a FOURTH reset at 96,953.0 while holding 3.33e174 energy, a third of the price, then needed 3,716 game-s more (More Layers at 100,668.6). ×3 did the same at 95,824.1 (4.79e173 held) and ×2 at 95,374.1 (6.94e172). So the score is a race between two thresholds, the cash-in rule's next gain and the fixed energy price, and losing it narrowly throws away 3,000-4,600 game-s of energy: that is the chaos between neighbouring ratios. At the four starts measured the race comes out the same way for each ratio, so the ratios' ORDER is the same at every start.

recommendation.verdict: switch it on at ×4 (the user's call)
recommendation.why: ×4 is the best ratio at all four starts (8th Quirk Layer at 97,673.05-98,242.5 against ×2 99,452.15-99,976.05: 1,732.7-2,303 game-s sooner, mean 1,875.3) and ends 104,000 with 10^0.51 more total quirks; ×5 is second at every start (1,181.65-1,776.35 sooner); the ratios fall in the same order at every start (×4 < ×5 < ×2 ≈ ×3 < ×3.5). The unevenness is in the RATIO, not the start: a race against More Layers' fixed price that ×4 and ×5 win and ×2, ×3, ×3.5 lose at every start here.
recommendation.caveats: All four starts are within 4,328 game-s before the switch and are perturbations of one trajectory; a change to the table BEFORE Improvement Boost could move the race. A ratio is a proxy for the real rule: do not cash in a quirk run whose energy is close to More Layers' price. A gate saying exactly that would be robust by construction — the next slice's retune candidate, not measured here.
